traits.capsule_ripe_months.note: Fitted to photos (no flora gives months for this region): Washington iNaturalist photos of T. muralis (imagekit batch moss-pnw-2026-11-05), tallied by the month each was taken, show ripe brown capsules in months 4, 5, young green ones in the months before and spent setae after.

traits.note: FNA vol. 27, Tortula (Zander and Eckel; efloras, read 2026-11-05): plants forming cushions, green, yellow-brown to dark brown below; stems usually to 2 cm; leaves appressed-incurved to lax when dry, spreading when moist, obovate to elliptic, 1-4(-6) mm; costa short- to long-excurrent as an awn; Tortula species delicate, characteristically light green, with smooth awns. Typical values are T. muralis, the wall moss (same volume): leaves short- to long-awned; seta 0.6-1.5 cm; capsule cylindric, erect, urn 1.5-2.7 mm; calcareous rock, often bricks or walls. Wikipedia, Tortula muralis (read 2026-11-05): greyish-green cushions no more than 1 cm tall; on concrete, brick walls, rock.

traits.leaf_shape.note: FNA vol. 27, Tortula (efloras, read 2026-11-05): leaves obovate to spathulate, ovate to elliptical, occasionally ligulate; the first word taken.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: About two fifths of the leaf's length, as FNA's obovate to elliptic blades (Tortula).

traits.capsule_share.note: T. muralis is autoicous and its sporophytes are commonly seen on walls (FNA vol. 27); the share, of shoots, is an estimate.

traits.colony_spread_m_per_year.note: Estimate for small wall cushions; to check against Glime, Bryophyte Ecology, vol. 1, chapter 5.

traits.operculum_form.note: FNA vol. 27, Tortula: operculum long-conic, occasionally shortly rostrate. (efloras, read 2026-11-05)

traits.older_leaf_colour.note: FNA vol. 27, Tortula muralis (read 2026-11-05): cushions green, yellow-brown to dark brown below. The colour is ours for that brown.

traits.leaf_colour.note: Hue measured: imagekit run moss-colour-2026-11-05 on batch moss-pnw-2026-11-05 (iNaturalist research-grade photos from Washington, about 20 a taxon, script moss_colour.py): the median linear r/g and b/g of the moss pixels (T. muralis r/g 1.02, b/g 0.30). Photos are exposed brighter than moss is, so only the hue is taken from them; the brightness is a green reflectance of 0.13, a lit leaf's, just above the 0.05-0.11 moss canopies reflect in the visible (Lovelock and Robinson 2002, Plant Cell Environ. 25: 1239, Antarctic Grimmia; moss biocrust albedo about 0.11 against 0.20 for bare soil, Sci. Total Environ. 2020), the canopy's own shade darkening the shell further.

traits.spore_diameter_m.note: FNA vol. 27, Tortula muralis (Zander and Eckel; efloras, read 2026-11-07): spores 8-12 µm, spheric; the genus's spores run 13-30(-50) µm in other species.

traits.cushion_breadth.note: Fitted to photos by eye (Jay chose it 2026-11-08, no flora gives a breadth): Washington iNaturalist photos of T. muralis (imagekit batch moss-pnw-2026-11-05) show cushions on walls and concrete about three times as wide as high; FNA vol. 27 says forming cushions, Wikipedia no more than 1 cm tall.
